cases.question: Trace how this Axios snapshot stores request/response interceptors and executes them around request dispatch. Explain registration/removal and IDs, runWhen eligibility, request/response ordering, synchronous-mode selection, callback results and errors, and the exact boundary for attaching response handlers. Compare the synchronous loop with the Promise chain rather than treating them as interchangeable. Assume ordinary manager records, callable fulfilled handlers, valid configurations, non-throwing runWhen predicates, and no changes to registration while a request is being constructed. Synchronous fulfilled handlers return configuration objects when successful; request rejection callbacks may be missing or throw. Stay at the manager, request assembly and public request error boundary: do not enumerate transport/adapter, configuration-merge, transformation or stack-formatting internals, and do not run the repository. For each finding, cite one representative implementation mechanism in a single contiguous range of at most 40 lines; explanations may synthesize other inspected branches without stitching quotations. Evidence boundary: read repository files with ordinary source tools; do not read parent-directory case catalogs, rubrics, controls, other trial artifacts, or any other private experiment files. In the Columbus condition only, the explicitly supplied frozen runtime skill/references and saved graph are also allowed; baseline must not inspect them.

findings.description: Explain the interceptor manager's own storage, option defaults and registration ID; how eject and clear affect slots, subsequent IDs and iteration. Cite how registration returns its ID.

Explain when and with which configuration runWhen is evaluated, its precise skipping test, exclusion from mode selection, the all/empty eligible-request rule, request versus response ordering, and whether response options affect selection. Cite how request callback pairs are inserted into the chain.

Explain Promise-path initialization and request/dispatch/response order, forwarding returned values or promises, rejection/recovery, and whether a fulfilled callback's own paired rejection callback catches its throw. Cite the iteration that attaches the Promise stages.

Explain direct fulfilled execution and config replacement; its own rejection callback's receiver, return-value handling, stopping behavior and surviving mutations; and whether a missing/throwing rejection callback reaches dispatch/response handlers or rejects the public request. Cite the synchronous loop's rejection-callback invocation.

Explain response-handler ordering and result/error flow after normally returned dispatch, comparing an asynchronously rejected dispatch promise with a synchronous dispatch throw in each request mode. Explain recovery and the final public outcome; cite the synchronous dispatch catch and response-chain attachment.
